chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluyah (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: My uncle Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim narrated to me, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Mansur ibn al-Abbas, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Ahmad ibn al-Jabbar, from his grandfather, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:
The gift is of three types: a gift in return (for a gift received), a gift for conciliation/friendship, and a gift for the sake of God, the Exalted.

key_terms.لِلَّهِ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ: For the sake of God, as an act of pure devotion
key_terms.مُصَانَعَةٍ: Gift for conciliation, friendship, or social bonding
key_terms.مُكَافَأَةٍ: Gift in return for a received gift or favor

ai.seo_question: What are the three types of gifts in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Khisal*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) delineates the spiritual taxonomy of gift-giving, distinguishing between social reciprocity (*mukafaha*), diplomatic conciliation (*musanafa*), and pure devotion (*li-llah*). This classification highlights the Shia emphasis on intention (*niyyah*) in transforming mundane social interactions into acts of worship, a concept central to the chapter's theme of identifying traits beloved or detested by God. The third category elevates the gift from a social transaction to a direct offering to the Divine, reflecting the Sufi-influenced yet jurisprudentially grounded Shia view of *ihsan* in interpersonal relations.
